newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds rose across the board in quiet trading on Tuesday following reports the Bank of Israel may raise the reserve requirement, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.16 pct to 101.21
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct to 100.72
Volume was low at 133 million shekels with turnover in the Makam falling to only 29 million shekels.
"Unlinked bonds rose today as they are expected to become more attractive if the central bank decides to raise the reserve requirement," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House.
Financial sources said on Tuesday the Bank of Israel may raise the reserve requirement for commercial banks in an effort to combat growing liquidity in the economy,

One source, confirming a report in the daily newspaper Haaretz this morning, said the central bank was considering raising the reserve requirement by five percentage points. That would raise the requirement to between eight and 11 percent, depending on the term of the deposit.

"Inflation-linked long bonds were rising today while other CPI-linked bonds were very mixed," said another trader. Traders noted that activity in CPI-linked bonds was relatively low at 32 million shekels.
Dollar-linked bonds rose sharply following the decline of the shekel against the dollar on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
